title: Stage 2 outputs and exit evidence
objective: List evidence missing when an opportunity says 'Visioning done' but has no use case owners.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Stage progress should reflect evidence, not a completed calendar event. "We held the Visioning workshop" is an activity. "We have three prioritized use cases with named owners and draft success measures" is evidence.

Glean's stage guidance describes the purpose of Stage 2 as use case workshops and visioning that lock scope, define Positive Business Outcomes (PBOs), and align on timeline and decision criteria. By the end of the stage, the account team should be able to show:

items: A champion, and the department and primary use cases in scope.
The problem in the customer's own words, plus the three whys.
Required capabilities: what must be true for the solution to succeed.
The future state: how the work changes and which outcomes it supports.
A mutual action plan (MAP) that the customer has seen and accepted.

blocks.x: An evidence pack, not a checkbox

blocks.x: The account team owns the exact required CRM fields. Partners contribute evidence; they are not tested on internal systems.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Don't mark a stage complete just because a workshop happened. If priorities or stakeholders are still unclear, assign focused follow-up before moving on.
Run the right number of sessions

Glean's training is explicit that Stage 2 isn't one size fits all. For a corporate account, Visioning may be a single 45- to 60-minute session. Commercial, enterprise, and strategic accounts may need several sessions, sometimes one per department head, before the priorities are clear. A strategic, wall-to-wall evaluation usually runs several DITL interviews as well.
Whatever the number of sessions, the exit evidence is the same: agreed priorities, owners, workflow maps, draft metrics, known dependencies, and a booked executive decision.

blocks.title: The Stage 2 evidence pack
blocks.alt: Six cards listing the evidence Stage 2 should leave behind: a use case log and matrix, a named owner per use case, current and future workflow maps, metric definitions and draft baselines, data and connector dependencies, and a scheduled executive decision meeting.
